en.title: Julian Alps lead Slovenia's snow: 40 cm in three days
en.description: Slovenia's mountains gained 1880 km² of snow cover in three days. The Julian Alps saw the most fall, with 40 cm, while lower ranges stayed dry.
en.lede: In the past three days, snow fell unevenly across Slovenia. The Julian Alps caught the heaviest snow, while lower mountains and foothills saw little or none.

p: When I look at where the snow fell, the pattern is sharp. The Julian Alps, in the north-west, took 40 cm in the last three days. The Kamnik-Savinja Alps, running east of there, received 31 cm. Pohorje, further south and lower, got only 12 cm. The same storm system moved over all three, but height made the difference.

This is typical for Slovenia in autumn. Moist air from the south hits the high ranges first and loses its snow there. By the time it reaches lower ground, it has less to give. Right now, 26 per cent of the modelled area is white, but almost all of it is above 1500 metres.

Above 1500 metres, the snow is real: 18 cm on average between 1500 and 2000 metres, and 35 cm above 2000 metres. Both bands are fully covered. Below 1500 metres, it thins fast. Between 1000 and 1500 metres, you will find only 2 cm on average, and snow covers just 60 per cent of the land. Below 1000 metres, almost nothing remains.

The snow line sits around 1200 metres today. That means most ski runs in the lower resorts are bare or will show stone through thin cover. At Sella Nevea, which sits highest at 2137 metres, snow depth is 42 cm. At Pokljuka, 1564 metres, it is 35 cm. At Kranjska Gora, only 1568 metres but catching less fresh snow, it is 25 cm.

The deepest snow is at Sella Nevea, 42 cm. It also caught the most fresh snow in three days, 26 cm. But Vogel, which sits higher at 1731 metres, picked up 33 cm of new snow and now holds 32 cm. Pokljuka received 31 cm of fresh fall in three days, the second-highest, and has 35 cm on the ground. These three are the only resorts with usable depth right now.

Kranjska Gora and Golte both sit around 1570 metres but face a harder time. Kranjska Gora has 25 cm and saw only 18 cm of new snow. Golte received 13 cm and holds 25 cm. Both caught the edge of the heaviest falls. Of the 27 ski areas we track in Slovenia, 16 now report some snow cover, but most of it lies above the main runs.

More snow is on the way. The forecast shows 23 cm possible in the next three days, with 23 November as the snowiest day. That is not a large amount for one day, but it will help. In the week ahead, up to 37 cm could fall. In the second week, from 30 November to 6 December, only 14 cm is expected, so the next ten days are your best window for accumulation.

The Julian Alps should see the heaviest snow again next week. If you are planning to ski, aim for dates around 25 November and into the first week of December. Lower resorts will benefit from each fall, but runs above 1500 metres will always have the best base.

sections.h: How this season is shaping up
p: Three weeks ago, only 1110 km² of Slovenia's ski terrain held snow. Yesterday, that was 750 km². Today it is 1880 km², a jump of 1130 km² in one day. The snow cover has surged, but it is still far below the total area we model (7340 km²). Early season snow is fragile and often patchy.

Compared to past winters, Sella Nevea is well ahead of normal for late November. It holds 42 cm against a typical 4 cm this date, nearly nine times the usual amount. Pokljuka, Vogel, Kranjska Gora and Golte are also above normal. But for a full season to build, Slovenia needs consistent falls through December and January. These first weeks matter, but they are only the start.

If you plan to ski off the main runs in coming days, check the latest avalanche bulletin from the official Slovenian service. Fresh snow on steep slopes always carries risk, especially when it falls fast. The snow is still settling in the high mountains. Wait a few days for it to stabilize, or stick to marked runs where the base is building.
Use the SnowScope app to track depth and forecast changes at your chosen resort. The mountains here move fast in autumn. In a week, the picture could change again.

advice: Aim for the Julian Alps and Kamnik-Savinja Alps resorts—Sella Nevea, Pokljuka, and Vogel—where fresh snow is deepest and new snow is thickest on the ground.
Stay above 1500 metres if you want continuous snow cover; below that height, runs are thin and stones may show through, especially on south-facing slopes.
Watch the forecast for 25 November and the first week of December, when the next significant snow is due. Early season snow can shrink fast in warm spells.
Check the official Slovenian avalanche bulletin before heading off-piste. Fresh snow of 30 cm or more on steep terrain can be unstable for several days after it falls.
Lower resorts like Kranjska Gora and Golte will improve as more snow falls, but they remain secondary until November passes and December snow sets a deeper base.

sl.title: Julijske Alpe vodijo Slovenijo v snega: 40 cm v treh dneh
sl.description: Slovenske gore so dobile 1880 km² snežne pokrivnosti v treh dneh. Julijske Alpe so dobile največ snega, 40 cm, nižja območja pa so ostala brez snega.
sl.lede: V zadnjih treh dneh je v Sloveniji padal sneg neenakomerno. Julijske Alpe so dobile največ snega, nižje gore in hribovja pa so ostale brez ali z malo snega.

sections.h: Tri gorske verige, tri različne zgodbe
p: Ko gledam, kje je padal sneg, je slika jasna. Julijske Alpe na severozahodu so v zadnjih treh dneh dobile 40 cm. Kamniško-savinjske Alpe, ki se razprostirajo vzhodno od tam, so dobile 31 cm. Pohorje, ki je dalje južno in nižje, je dobilo le 12 cm. Isti vremenski sistem se je premaknil čez vse tri, a nadmorska višina je naredila razliko.

To je v jeseni v Sloveniji tipično. Vlažen zrak z juga se najprej trka ob visoke gorske verige in tam izgubi sneg. Ko doseže nižje ozemlje, ima manj snega za oddajo. Trenutno je 26 odstotkov modeliranega območja belo, vendar je skoraj vse nad 1500 metri.

Nad 1500 metri je sneg pravi: v povprečju 18 cm med 1500 in 2000 metri ter 35 cm nad 2000 metri. Obe višinski pasu sta v celoti prekrita. Pod 1500 metri se sneg hitro tanjša. Med 1000 in 1500 metri boste našli v povprečju le 2 cm, sneg pa pokriva le 60 odstotkov ozemlja. Pod 1000 metri skoraj nič ne ostane.

Snežna meja se danes nahaja približno na 1200 metrih. To pomeni, da so večina smučarskih prog v nižjih postajah brez snega ali bodo pokazale kamen skozi tanko pokrivnost. Na Sella Nevea, ki se nahaja najvišje na 2137 metrih, je globina snega 42 cm. Na Pokljuki, 1564 metra, je 35 cm. Na Kranjski Gori, le 1568 metra visoko, a s prejemanjem manjše količine svežega snega, je 25 cm.

Najgloblejši sneg je na Sella Nevea, 42 cm. Tam je tudi padlo največ svežega snega v treh dneh, 26 cm. Toda Vogel, ki se nahaja višje na 1731 metrih, je prejel 33 cm novega snega in ima zdaj 32 cm snega na tleh. Pokljuka je v treh dneh prejela 31 cm svežega snega, drugo največjo količino, in ima 35 cm snega na tleh. Te tri postaje so edine s pravzaprav uporabno globino trenutno.

Kranjska Gora in Golte se obe nahajata okoli 1570 metrih, a sta v težjih razmerah. Kranjska Gora ima 25 cm in je dobila le 18 cm novega snega. Golte je prejela 13 cm in ima 25 cm. Obe sta dosegli rob najhujšega padavanja. Od 27 smučarskih območij, ki jih spremljamo v Sloveniji, jih 16 zdaj poroča neko snežno pokrivnost, vendar večina leži nad glavnimi progami.

Več snega je na poti. Napoved kaže 23 cm možnega snega v naslednjih treh dneh, pri čemer je 23. november najbolj snežni dan. To ni velika količina za en dan, toda pomoč bo. V naslednjem tednu bi lahko padlo do 37 cm. V drugem tednu, od 30. novembra do 6. decembra, se pričakuje le 14 cm, zato so naslednji deset dni vaše najboljše okno za kopičenje snega.

Julijske Alpe bi naj ponovno videle največ snega naslednji teden. Če načrtujete smučanje, si zastavite roke oko 25. novembra in v prvi teden decembra. Nižje postaje bodo koristile od vsakega padavanja, toda proge nad 1500 metri bodo vedno imele najboljšo podlago.

Pred tremi tedni je le 1110 km² slovenskega smučarskega terena imelo sneg. Včeraj je bilo 750 km². Danes je 1880 km², skok za 1130 km² v enem dnevu. Snežna pokrivnost je narasla, toda je še vedno daleko pod skupnim območjem, ki ga modeliramo (7340 km²). Začetni sneg je krhek in pogosto neenakomeren.

V primerjavi s prejšnjimi zimami je Sella Nevea dobro pred normalnim stanjem za konec novembra. Ima 42 cm v primerjavi s tipičnimi 4 cm na ta datum, skoraj devetkrat običajno količino. Pokljuka, Vogel, Kranjska Gora in Golte so tudi nad normalnim stanjem. Toda da se sezono v celoti izgradi, potrebuje Slovenija dosledne padavine v decembru in januarju. Ti prvi tedni so važni, toda le začetek.

Če načrtujete smučanje izven glavnih prog v naslednjih dneh, preverite najnovejši plazovni bilten uradne slovenske službe. Svež sneg na strmih pobočjih vedno nosi tveganje, še posebej ko pada hitro. Sneg se še vedno usedlja v visokih gorah. Počakajte nekaj dni, da se stabilizira, ali se držite označenih prog, kjer se podlaga gradi.
Uporabite aplikacijo SnowScope za spremljanje globine in napovedi sprememb na vaši izbrani postaji. Gore tukaj se premikajo hitro v jeseni. V tednu bi se slika lahko ponovno spremenila.

advice: Cilje na postaje Julijskih Alp in Kamniško-savinjskih Alp—Sella Nevea, Pokljuka in Vogel—kjer je svež sneg najglobji in novo padani sneg najdebelejši na tleh.
Ostanite nad 1500 metri, če želite neprekinjeno snežno pokrivnost; pod to višino so proge tanke in kamen lahko prleska skozi, posebej na jugu obrnjenih pobočjih.
Spremljajte napoved za 25. november in prvi teden decembra, ko je naslednji pomemben sneg predviden. Začetni sneg se lahko hitro skrajša v toplih obdobjih.
Preverite uradni slovenski plazovni bilten, preden se podате v terenu izven poti. Svež sneg 30 cm ali več na strmem terenu je lahko nestabilen več dni po padacu.
Nižje postaje, kot sta Kranjska Gora in Golte, se bodo izboljšale, ko bo padlo več snega, toda ostajajo drugo izbiro do konca novembra in dokler december ne položi globljo podlago.
